summary: A round that uses up a whole side face must make a full round, not be refused (#199). A 14 x 6 x 10 bar has its four vertical edges rounded r 3: both 6 mm end faces are used up, each end becomes a half cylinder. With one end only, two rounds meet on that end face. A 6 x 6 x 10 post rounded r 3 on all four vertical edges is a cylinder of radius 3. Closed-form volumes; SolidCraft checked 2e-4 relative on a mesh, these check 1e-4 mm^3. The test's past-the-limit sizes (3.001, 3.5) must be refused (expect.refused); 3.5 needs fillet_refuse_crossing_rails, without which the pinned SMLib returns an empty, non-manifold body. With the generic blend's checks (`fillet_gn_section_generator`, `fillet_refuse_overlapping_bands`) the refusals report the largest radius that builds, 3 (expect.refused.fit_size).

cases.name: round_past_the_end_face_is_refused
cases.note: r 3.001 on the four vertical edges: past the 6 mm end faces, which have nothing left to use up. SolidCraft refuses it as larger than the neighbouring faces; so does solidcore, with the default flags and with every flag.

cases.name: round_well_past_the_end_face_is_refused
cases.note: r 3.5 on the four vertical edges. With the default flags the pinned SMLib returns success with a non-manifold body and all of the bar's volume gone (WR-460); fillet_refuse_crossing_rails refuses it.

cases.name: round_3_001_refused_with_its_fit
cases.note: r 3.001 on the four vertical edges with the generic blend's fold and room checks: refused, and the largest radius that builds, 3 (half the 6 mm end face), comes back on the refusal (WR-696, tangency-labs/solidcore#2278).
